title: SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission
funding_type: Subsidised tuition coverage + living, accommodation and one-off allowances (university-administered)
administering_authority: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
implementing_agency: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) - Office of Student Administration / SUTD Scholarships Office
programme_action: SUTD-administered undergraduate scholarship for Singapore Permanent Residents and international students of Asian nationality (Singapore Citizens excluded)
description: The SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship is a SUTD-administered undergraduate scholarship offered to outstanding Asian students (excluding Singapore Citizens) who are admitted to full-time MOE-subsidised SUTD degree programmes leading to a first degree in Bachelor of Engineering (Engineering Product Development, Engineering Systems and Design or Computer Science and Design) or Bachelor of Science (Design and Artificial Intelligence). It covers the subsidised tuition fees payable after the MOE Tuition Grant for the normal duration of up to four years, plus a living allowance of S$6,000 per academic year, an annual accommodation allowance equivalent to the lowest on-campus double-room rate, a one-off settling-in allowance of S$200, a one-off computer allowance of S$1,750, and one-way and return air passages. There is no separate scholarship application: applicants indicate their interest in SUTD scholarships inside the single SUTD admission application, and admission and scholarship are evaluated together. The award carries a six-year service bond with a Singapore-registered company, in addition to the three-year MOE Tuition Grant work bond that applies to all Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who take up the Tuition Grant.

award_types: SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship (tuition + living allowance + accommodation allowance + one-off allowances + air passage + six-year bond)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: One award type only. Sibling SUTD-administered awards open to international undergraduates are listed separately: SUTD Rainmaker (International) Scholarship, SUTD Trailblazers (International) Scholarship, ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship, and donor scholarships such as the Regent Group - SUTD Scholarship (ASEAN nations). Applicants may indicate interest in SUTD-administered scholarships generally rather than in one named award.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Pass all subjects in Term 1 and maintain a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 3.5 out of 5.0 from Term 2 onwards; academic performance is reviewed every term. Overseas exchange is limited to no more than two terms (six months). Recipients must complete at least 20 hours of service to the University. Concurrent holding of any other scholarship, bursary or university loan requires University approval. The scholarship may be withdrawn at any time if academic progress or conduct is deemed unsatisfactory.
programme_structure.intake: Single annual undergraduate intake at SUTD; scholarship is considered with the admission application for the same intake.

verification_notes: Verified on 2026-10-03 against 11 official pages: the SUTD award page for the SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship, the SUTD-administered scholarships index, the SUTD undergraduate admissions page, the SUTD application guide, the SUTD tuition fees page, the SUTD Tuition Grant eligibility page, and four Ministry of Education Tuition Grant Scheme pages. application_deadline.deadline_timezone: Singapore Time (SGT, UTC+08:00); SUTD publishes calendar dates but no cut-off hour
application_deadline.typical_application_window: 2 January to 2 March 2026 for all qualifications other than Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level; from the release of A-Level results to 19 March 2026 for Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level. An equivalent window is expected around January to March each year.
application_deadline.application_period: AY2026 entry: 2 January 2026 - 2 March 2026 (all qualifications except Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level); Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level applicants: from release of A-Level results through 19 March 2026.
application_deadline.official_rule: SUTD does not publish a separate scholarship deadline. The scholarship is applied for at the same time as admission, so the admissions deadline applies: 'Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level qualification: from the day of release of A-Level results to 19 March 2026. All other qualifications: 2 January to 2 March 2026.' The recorded deadline_date is the later of the two 2026 dates; international-qualification applicants faced 2 March 2026.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The recorded deadline_date is the closed 2026-cycle date and is kept for reference only. The AY2027 window has not been published as of 2026-10-03; do not assume the same dates.

programme_duration.official_range: Normal duration of up to four years
programme_duration.renewal_note: SUTD describes the coverage as applying 'for the normal duration (up to four years)' of the respective degree programmes. Students pay fees for 8 academic terms, i.e. the normal course duration. Renewal each term depends on passing all subjects in Term 1 and maintaining a CGPA of 3.5 out of 5.0 from Term 2 onwards.

funding.scholarship_type: University-administered merit scholarship considered with the admission application (no separate scholarship form)
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend or monthly amount is published. The only recurring cash allowance is S$6,000 per academic year.
funding.travel_amount_note: The award covers one-way air passage from the home country to Singapore at the beginning of the course and return air passage from Singapore to the home country at the end of the course, but SUTD publishes no monetary value for it.
funding.institutional_costs: Subsidised tuition fees payable after the MOE Tuition Grant are covered for the normal duration of up to four years. Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees and any fees beyond the subsidised rate are not covered.
funding.fully_funded_note: The award covers subsidised tuition, a S$6,000 per-academic-year living allowance, an accommodation allowance, a S$200 settling-in allowance, a S$1,750 computer allowance and air passages, but it is not an unconditional full ride: Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees are not covered, recipients who do not take up the MOE Tuition Grant pay non-subsidised fees, and the award carries a six-year SUTD service bond layered on top of the three-year MOE Tuition Grant work bond.

tuition.conditions: Covers the subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant) for the normal duration of up to four years. For AY2026 new students the subsidised fee payable is S$30,200 per academic year for ASEAN International Students and S$31,600 per academic year for all other International Students (both inclusive of 9% GST); Singapore Permanent Residents pay S$19,350 per academic year. Recipients who do not take up the Tuition Grant pay the non-subsidised fee of S$62,076 per academic year and are not covered.

travel_allowance.conditions: One-way air passage from home country to Singapore at the beginning of the course of study and return air passage from Singapore to home country at the end of the course. No S$ value is published.

insurance.note: Not published as a scholarship benefit. Student insurance under the SUTD Student Insurance Scheme is paid for through Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees, which are not covered by the award.

research_allowance.note: Not published in official source for this award

book_allowance.note: Not published in official source for this award

equipment_allowance.conditions: One-off computer allowance upon matriculation, for recipients matriculating from AY2022 onwards.

accommodation_support.conditions: Annual accommodation allowance equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation. SUTD does not publish the S$ figure or the underlying room rate on the award page.

bond.scholarship_bond: Six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately upon graduation.
bond.government_bond: Recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme. Singapore Permanent Residents and international students under the Tuition Grant must serve a 3-year bond after graduation (Tier C for international students, competitive and merit-based, limited numbers).
bond.note: Both bonds apply. Applicants who decline the MOE Tuition Grant lose access to subsidised fees and therefore to the tuition benefit.

total_estimated_value.note: SUTD does not publish a total award value; components are published separately.

coverage: Subsidised tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant) for the normal duration of up to four years
Living allowance of S$6,000 per academic year
Accommodation allowance per academic year equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation
One-off computer allowance of S$1,750 upon matriculation (recipients matriculating from AY2022 onwards)
One-way air passage from home country to Singapore at the start of the course and return air passage from Singapore to home country at the end of the course
coverage_limitations: Only the subsidised tuition fee payable after the MOE Tuition Grant is covered. Recipients who do not take up the Tuition Grant pay non-subsidised fees of S$62,076 per academic year (AY2026) and are not covered.

Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees are not covered: a one-time S$10 enrolment fee to student activities and services plus S$165 per term for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents and S$232 per term for International Students in AY2026 (inclusive of 9% GST).
The accommodation allowance is capped at the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation; SUTD publishes no S$ figure, and any difference for a higher-rated room is borne by the student.
No book allowance, insurance, visa support, research allowance or family allowance is published for this award.
The living allowance is S$6,000 per academic year, which is modest against Singapore living costs.

The award is not unconditional: a six-year SUTD service bond with a Singapore-registered company applies, plus the three-year MOE Tuition Grant work obligation, plus liquidated damages on premature termination or breach.
Overseas exchange is restricted to no more than two terms (six months) during the course of study.
The exact benefit structure for future intakes may differ; SUTD revises allowances and fees by cohort and publishes figures per academic year.

final_year_condition: For this undergraduate award the relevant qualification is secondary/high-school completion: final-year secondary-school students may apply in the standard admissions window on the strength of Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Local Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications. SUTD's application guide requires applicants to upload academic transcripts and certificates at secondary/junior high and senior high school levels and to key in any supplementary results where required. The scholarship funds the bachelor's degree itself, so there is no 'final year of bachelor' rule.
equivalent_degree_note: SUTD's admissions route for International applicants explicitly lists non-Singaporean school-leaving qualifications including A-Level Certifications (International), Australian Qualifications, India Standard 12, Indonesia Ijazah SMA, Indonesian Ujian Nasional (UN), International Baccalaureate Diploma (International), Malaysia Unified Examination Certificate (UEC), Myanmar Matriculation Examination (MME), Philippines High School Certificate, PRC National College Entrance Exam (NCEE), Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM), Thailand Certificate of Secondary Education (Mathayom 6), US High School Diploma, Vietnam High School Graduation Examination, and Other International Qualifications. The award page requires 'outstanding ... or Year 12 equivalent qualifications'.
nationality_quota: Limited to Singapore Permanent Residents and International Students of an Asian country or region nationality (Singapore Citizens excluded). No numeric quota or number of awards is published.
previous_award_restriction: Recipients may not, without the approval of the University, hold concurrently any other scholarships, bursaries or university loans. MOE Tuition Grant eligibility additionally requires that the student has not previously taken a Tuition Grant or received Government of Singapore sponsorship/scholarship to attain another qualification at an equal or higher level; a student who already received a Tuition Grant is eligible only up to the normal course duration less the number of terms already received. Polytechnic-grant holders who are not discharged from a previous Tuition Grant bond must sign a Supplementary Agreement.

application_method.application_route: No separate scholarship application exists. Applicants submit one application through the SUTD Admissions System and indicate interest in SUTD-administered scholarships within the 'Scholarships and financial aid' section; admission and scholarship are then evaluated together.
application_steps: Review SUTD admission requirements and the international qualification list for your country.
Create one application in the SUTD Admissions System (duplicate applications are not processed).
Complete personal particulars, uploading the front and back of the NRIC (Singapore Citizens/SPRs) or the passport particulars page (International Students).
Provide contact information with a valid email address valid for at least 12 months from registration.
Enter academic grades and upload academic transcripts and certificates at secondary/junior high and senior high school levels.
Where required for your qualification, key in and upload supplementary results such as an English proficiency test.
List up to two referees and upload school or other relevant testimonial/recommendation letters.
List outstanding and relevant achievements (leadership, research/internship/entrepreneurship, community service, significant achievements) within the last four years, and upload supporting documents.
In the 'Scholarships and financial aid' section, declare gross monthly household income and indicate that you wish to apply for SUTD-administered scholarships, then answer the supporting questions.
For Singapore Permanent Residents and International Students, indicate the intention to apply for the MOE Tuition Grant.
Submit the declaration that the information provided is accurate.

If offered a place with Tuition Grant, accept the offer, register at the MOE TG&S website in early September with two guarantors aged 21-65 who are not undischarged bankrupts, and complete electronic signing of the Tuition Grant Agreement.
If shortlisted, respond to SUTD notification; the specific scholarship awarded is communicated with the admission offer.

degree_outcome.degree_note: Only SUTD degree programmes leading to a first degree in the listed majors are eligible for this award; other SUTD degrees are funded through the sibling awards listed on the SUTD scholarships page.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Subsidised tuition fees payable after the MOE Tuition Grant are covered for the normal duration of up to four years. For AY2026 new students the subsidised fee is S$30,200 per academic year for ASEAN International Students and S$31,600 per academic year for all other International Students (both inclusive of 9% GST); Singapore Permanent Residents pay S$19,350 per academic year. SUTD uses a cohort-based fixed fee model, so the fee for a cohort stays unchanged through the normal candidature. Students who do not sign the Tuition Grant Agreement or are not eligible for the grant pay the non-subsidised fee of S$62,076 per academic year.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Recipients are bound by the SUTD scholarship terms and conditions. Those who take up the MOE Tuition Grant must sign the Tuition Grant Agreement electronically with two guarantors of any nationality aged 21 and above but below 65 who are not undischarged bankrupts; Polytechnic Tuition Grant holders who are not discharged from a previous bond must also sign a Supplementary Agreement.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees are payable by all students and are not covered by the award: a one-time S$10 enrolment fee to student activities and services plus S$165.00 per term for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents and S$232.00 per term for International Students in AY2026 (inclusive of 9% GST). Insurance coverage under the SUTD Student Insurance Scheme is delivered through these fees. TFL and Study Loans do not cover Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees or hostel fees, and do not cover the tuition fees of SPRs and IS in full because the loan amount is capped at the subsidised tuition fees for Singapore Citizens.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: Two overlapping obligations. (1) MOE Tuition Grant Scheme: Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who take up the Tuition Grant must serve a 3-year bond after graduation, i.e. be employed full-time in a Singapore entity for 3 years. International students may apply only for a Tier C Tuition Grant, which is limited in number, competitive and merit-based. (2) SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship: recipients are required to serve a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately upon graduation.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: MOE: liquidated damages must be paid if there are changes to course status or if the bond is bought out; bond deferment can be applied for through the TG&S Portal. SUTD: if the recipient terminates the scholarship prematurely or breaches any of the terms and conditions, the recipient is liable to pay liquidated damages equivalent to the amount received from the commencement of the scholarship until its termination, plus 10% compounded interest per annum.

motivation_letter_strategy: SUTD asks for personal insight questions rather than a single motivation letter, so use those responses to evidence the specific attributes the award names: exemplary Co-Curricular Activities records and good leadership qualities and potential.
Because admission and scholarship are evaluated together, the same application carries both outcomes - do not treat scholarship evidence as an optional extra.

The application guide asks for leadership, research, internship, entrepreneurship, community service and significant achievements within the last four years, so prioritise recent, verifiable and specific evidence over old or generic claims.

SUTD is a design- and technology-focused university with a Design.AI curriculum; align your narrative with design, technology and interdisciplinary problem-solving rather than a generic engineering statement.
Optional URLs to videos may be submitted; only use them if they add information the written responses cannot carry.

Submitting duplicate applications, which SUTD states will not be processed
Budgeting for the non-subsidised fee and assuming the scholarship removes it - the scholarship covers only the subsidised fee after the Tuition Grant
Overlooking Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees, which are payable regardless of the scholarship
Ignoring the six-year SUTD service bond and the three-year MOE Tuition Grant work obligation
Applying after the admissions window closes - the scholarship has no independent window
Holding another scholarship, bursary or university loan concurrently without University approval
Planning more than two terms (six months) of overseas exchange, which the terms disallow
Assuming Singapore Citizens are eligible; they are explicitly excluded from this award and are covered by the Singaporean awards list

risk_flags.risk: The assigned target named awards ('SUTD Global Undergraduate Scholarship', 'Darusshahdan Chair Scholars') that do not exist on the current official SUTD site, so the record was substituted for the SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship.
risk_flags.impact: The record does not describe the award the task originally named; users searching for the legacy names will not find a match.
risk_flags.mitigation: The substitution is stated in database_notes and verification.unverified_or_removed_claims. The SUTD-administered scholarships index page is cited so users can see the full current list of international-eligible awards.

risk_flags.risk: The award page states no monetary value for the air-passage benefit and none for the accommodation allowance (it is expressed by reference to the lowest on-campus double-room rate).
risk_flags.impact: The total cash value of the award cannot be computed, and the accommodation benefit may be worth far less than applicants expect if room rates rise.
risk_flags.mitigation: Both are recorded as covered with amount null and an explanatory condition; no value was invented. Applicants should request the current lowest double-room rate from SUTD Housing.

risk_flags.risk: Two overlapping service bonds apply: a six-year SUTD bond and a three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond.
risk_flags.impact: A graduate who wants to leave Singapore faces two bond obligations and liquidated damages, so the award is not a free ride.
risk_flags.mitigation: Both bonds are recorded in funding_breakdown.bond and student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement, and fully_funded is set to false with an explanatory note.

risk_flags.risk: The MOE Tuition Grant for international students (Tier C) is limited in number, competitive and merit-based, and SUTD states there is a limited number available for international students.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant could be admitted without the Tuition Grant, in which case the tuition benefit does not apply and the non-subsidised fee of S$62,076 per academic year would be payable.
risk_flags.mitigation: The dependency is stated in the tuition conditions and coverage_limitations; the SUTD Tuition Grant eligibility page is cited for the application and signing requirements.

risk_flags.risk: Renewal requires passing all subjects in Term 1 and maintaining a CGPA of 3.5 out of 5.0 from Term 2 onwards, with review every term.
risk_flags.impact: A single weak term can end the award, and the terms allow withdrawal at any time for unsatisfactory progress or conduct.
risk_flags.mitigation: Renewal criteria are recorded in programme_structure.renewal_criteria and programme_duration.renewal_note, and the withdrawal clause is quoted in the coverage limitations and bond breach fields.

risk_flags.risk: SUTD revises tuition fees and allowances by cohort, and the award page carries no last-updated date.
risk_flags.impact: Benefit amounts published for AY2025 or AY2026 recipients may differ for the next intake.
risk_flags.mitigation: source_last_updated records the absence of a date; verification.programme_check_required lists allowance and fee changes for the next cycle, and next_verification_due is set to 2027-01-15.

risk_flags.risk: The application deadline is tied to the admissions window rather than to the scholarship, and the AY2027 window has not been published.
risk_flags.impact: Applicants who track only a 'scholarship deadline' may miss the admissions window entirely, because the scholarship has no independent window.
risk_flags.mitigation: The application_deadline object records both 2026 windows and explicitly states that no separate scholarship deadline exists. deadline_precision is set to exact for the recorded 2026 date, typical_application_window describes the recurring January-March pattern, and deadline_warning warns against assuming the same dates for AY2027.

risk_flags.risk: Concurrent holding of any other scholarship, bursary or university loan requires University approval.
risk_flags.impact: A recipient who stacks funding without approval risks withdrawal of the scholarship and liquidated damages.
risk_flags.mitigation: The restriction is recorded in previous_award_restriction, programme_structure.renewal_criteria and the common mistakes list; SUTD's own note that applicants may apply for both SUTD and donor scholarships is recorded alongside it.

best_fit: A high-achieving Singapore Permanent Resident or international student of Asian nationality (outside Singapore) with outstanding school-leaving results, an exemplary co-curricular record and demonstrated leadership potential, who is targeting a first degree in BEng (Engineering Product Development, Engineering Systems and Design or Computer Science and Design) or BSc (Design and Artificial Intelligence) at SUTD, and who accepts a six-year service bond with a Singapore-registered company and the three-year MOE Tuition Grant work obligation in Singapore.

Applicants who need master's or PhD funding

official_fields_confirmed: Official award name: SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship
Eligibility: Singapore Permanent Residents and International Students of an Asian country or region nationality except Singapore, with Singapore Citizens excluded

Eligible programmes: BEng majors in Engineering Product Development, Engineering Systems and Design, Computer Science and Design, and BSc major in Design and Artificial Intelligence, all full-time and MOE-subsidised
Entry qualifications: outstanding Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Local Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent
Selection factors: exemplary Co-Curricular Activities records, good leadership qualities and potential
Benefit: subsidised tuition fees after Tuition Grant for the normal duration of up to four years
Benefit: living allowance of S$6,000 per academic year
Benefit: accommodation allowance per academic year equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation
Benefit: one-off settling-in allowance of S$200
Benefit: one-off computer allowance of S$1,750 upon matriculation for recipients matriculating from AY2022 onwards
Benefit: one-way air passage from home country to Singapore at the beginning of the course and return air passage at the end
Bond: six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately upon graduation
Bond breach: liquidated damages equal to the amount received from commencement until termination plus 10% compounded interest per annum
Renewal: pass all subjects in Term 1 and maintain CGPA of 3.5 out of 5.0 from Term 2 onwards, reviewed every term
Service requirement: at least 20 hours of service to the University
Concurrent holding of other scholarships, bursaries or university loans prohibited without University approval
Overseas exchange limited to no more than two terms (six months)
Application made at the same time as application for admission; no separate scholarship application
MOE Tuition Grant Scheme: Singapore Permanent Residents and international students must serve a 3-year bond after graduation, employed full-time in a Singapore entity
MOE Tuition Grant: Tier C for international students, limited in number, competitive and merit-based; Tier B for Permanent Residents; Singapore Citizens receive Tier A automatically with no bond
MOE Tuition Grant registration: two guarantors of any nationality, aged 21 and above but below 65, not undischarged bankrupts; registration in early September and e-signing of the agreement
AY2026 subsidised tuition fees: S$13,500 (SC), S$19,350 (SPR), S$30,200 (ASEAN IS) and S$31,600 (all other IS) per academic year; non-subsidised S$62,076 per academic year
AY2026 Compulsory Miscellaneous Fees: S$10 one-time enrolment fee, S$165 per term (SC/SPR) and S$232 per term (IS)
2026 application windows: Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level from release of results to 19 March 2026; all other qualifications 2 January to 2 March 2026
Only one electronic application is accepted; duplicate applications are not processed
LOGO: official SUTD logo asset at https://www.sutd.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/SUTDLogo_Dark@2x.png, verified on the official domain and visually confirmed as the SUTD wordmark

database_notes: SUBSTITUTION: The assigned target named the 'SUTD Global Undergraduate Scholarship / SUTD Scholarship' and the 'Darusshahdan Chair Scholars'. Neither name appears on any official sutd.edu.sg page retrieved on 2026-10-03, including the SUTD-administered scholarships index. This record was substituted with the SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship, which is the established SUTD-administered undergraduate scholarship explicitly listed under 'For international students'. The filename slot was kept as instructed.

SIBLING AWARDS for comparison: the SUTD-administered scholarships index lists, for international students, the SUTD Rainmaker (International) Scholarship (open to all SPR/IS; subsidised tuition, S$10,000 annual allowance at S$5,000 per academic term, travel award up to S$5,000, no SUTD bond), the SUTD Trailblazers (International) Scholarship (subsidised tuition only, no SUTD bond), the SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship, the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship (ASEAN nationals except Singapore; S$5,800 living allowance, S$3,000 accommodation allowance, S$1,750 computer allowance, no bond), plus donor scholarships. Applicants may indicate interest in SUTD-administered scholarships generally rather than in one named award.

The SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship restricts eligibility to Singapore Permanent Residents and International Students of an Asian country or region nationality (except Singapore), so worldwide_eligibility is false and citizenship_restriction is true. No numeric quota is published.

Two bonds apply and must be read together: the SUTD scholarship's own six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company, and the MOE Tuition Grant's three-year work bond for Singapore Permanent Residents and international students. Because of the service bonds, fully_funded is set to false even though tuition, living, accommodation, settling-in, computer and airfare components are all covered.

The tuition benefit is defined as the subsidised fee payable after the MOE Tuition Grant, not the full non-subsidised fee. AY2026 subsidised fees per academic year are S$13,500 (SC), S$19,350 (SPR), S$30,200 (ASEAN IS) and S$31,600 (all other IS), all inclusive of 9% GST for the international-student categories; the non-subsidised fee is S$62,076 per academic year. These figures are recorded as context in student_rights_and_cost_protection and are not presented as the award amount.
The accommodation allowance and the air-passage benefit are published as entitlements without S$ values, so funding_breakdown records them as covered with amount null. No value was estimated.

Competitive and time-limited nature of the MOE Tier C Tuition Grant for international students is recorded as a risk: the scholarship's tuition benefit depends on the applicant actually receiving the grant.

No separate scholarship deadline exists. The 2026 admissions windows (2 January to 2 March 2026 for all qualifications other than Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level; from release of A-Level results to 19 March 2026 for GCE A-Level) are recorded in application_deadline. deadline_date is the later of the two 2026 dates for reference; both have passed as of 2026-10-03, hence status CLOSED.

SUTD does not publish an application fee for undergraduate admission on the pages reviewed, so application_method.application_fee and student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients are null rather than assumed to be zero.
No interview, portfolio requirement, or English test minimum is published for this award; these fields are null rather than inferred.
The SUTD application guide allows applicants to submit URLs to videos on social media websites as additional information; this is optional and is not treated as a portfolio requirement.

The logo is the official SUTD wordmark hosted on the sutd.edu.sg domain and rendered on the official scholarship page. It was downloaded and visually inspected on 2026-10-03. No award-specific photograph could be verified, so image_url is null.

SUTD's site metadata lists the scholarships index page as published 2024-09-23 and several award pages with 2026 publication dates, but no last-updated date is published on the SUTD Design and Engineering Scholarship page itself. This is recorded in source_last_updated rather than guessed.

Renewal CGPA (3.5 out of 5.0 from Term 2 onwards) is a continuation requirement, not an entry requirement. No entry GPA or percentage threshold is published, so academic_requirements.fixed_percentage_requirement is false and eligibility.gpa_requirement records only the continuation rule.

No CS/technical short-form acronym for the award could be verified on official pages; 'SUTD D&E Scholarship' is a descriptive short form created for the database and this is stated rather than implied.
